146	//  Swizzle mode (PTX ISA §<ip>.4, descriptor bits 62-61 "swizzle mode").
147	//
148	//  The shared-memory matrix descriptor encodes how the 128-bit core-matrix
149	//  rows are interleaved in smem to avoid bank conflicts on the wgmma read.
150	//  CRITICAL: the descriptor's layout_type field (bits 63:62) does NOT use a
151	//  size-ascending encoding. The hardware/CUTLASS encoding is
152	//  (cute/arch/mma_sm90_desc.hpp LayoutType, verified):
153	//    NONE/INTERLEAVE = 0,  SWIZZLE_128B = 1,  SWIZZLE_64B = 2,  SWIZZLE_32B = 3.
154	//  (An earlier draft had 32B=1/128B=3 swapped; the correctness path uses NONE=0
155	//  so it was unaffected, but the perf-phase swizzle modes MUST use these values.)
156	//
157	//  CORRECTNESS-PATH NOTE (deviation flagged in the report): the gated /
158	//  tested numerics path ships swizzle = NONE (kSwizzleNone). NONE is a
159	//  fully-legal descriptor mode (§<ip>.4) and is the layout the
160	//  correctness gates validate against torch. The 128B-swizzle layout is a
161	//  PERF-PHASE optimization (bank-conflict elimination on the smem read) and
162	//  is exposed here as the template parameter the model headers will select
163	//  once the quiet-GPU perf phase measures it; it is NOT required for any
164	//  correctness gate. See DESIGN §4.1 ("specify the 128-byte-swizzle layout"
165	//  is the perf target; phase-1 staging uses cp.async, §4.1 item 3).
166	// =========================================================================
167	enum SwizzleMode : uint32_t {
168	    kSwizzleNone = 0,   // INTERLEAVE / no swizzle (the correctness-path layout)
169	    kSwizzle128B = 1,   // SWIZZLE_128B
170	    kSwizzle64B  = 2,   // SWIZZLE_64B
171	    kSwizzle32B  = 3,   // SWIZZLE_32B

174	// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
175	//  generic-smem-pointer → matrix-descriptor start address.
176	//  PTX ISA §<ip>.4: the descriptor's bits 13-0 hold the start address of
177	//  the matrix in shared memory, encoded as the 18-bit smem byte address with
178	//  the low 4 bits dropped — i.e. addr_field = (smem_byte_addr & 0x3FFFF) >> 4.
179	//  The low 4 bits MUST be zero (16-byte alignment) or they are silently lost.
180	// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
181	__device__ __forceinline__ uint32_t smem_desc_encode_addr(const void* smem_ptr) {
182	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 900)
183	    uint32_t a = static_cast<uint32_t>(__cvta_generic_to_shared(smem_ptr));
184	    return (a & 0x3FFFFu) >> 4;
185	#else
186	    (void)smem_ptr;
187	    return 0u;
188	#endif
189	}

191	// =========================================================================
192	//  Shared-memory matrix descriptor (PTX ISA §<ip>.4).
193	//
194	//  64-bit layout (bit ranges per the ISA table):
195	//    bits  13: 0  start address (smem byte addr >> 4)
196	//    bits  15:14  (reserved / 0)
197	//    bits  29:16  leading-dimension byte offset (LBO) >> 4
198	//    bits  31:30  (reserved / 0)
199	//    bits  45:32  stride-dimension byte offset (SBO) >> 4
200	//    bits  48:46  (reserved / 0)
201	//    bits  51:49  matrix base offset (for swizzle; 0 for our tiles)
202	//    bits  61:52  (reserved / 0)
203	//    bits  63:62  swizzle / layout mode (0 none / 1 128B / 2 64B / 3 32B —
204	//                 the CUTLASS LayoutType encoding, see SwizzleMode above)
205	//
206	//  LBO and SBO are the byte offsets between consecutive "core matrices" along
207	//  the leading and stride dimensions respectively (§<ip>.3 "Strides").
208	//  Both are encoded >>4 (16-byte granular). The exact (LBO,SBO) depend on the
209	//  operand's smem tile layout; the make_desc_*_kmajor builders below compute
210	//  them for the canonical row-major-K bf16 tiles the model headers stage.
211	// =========================================================================
212	struct SmemDesc {
213	    uint64_t desc;
214	};
215	
216	// Low-level builder: caller supplies LBO/SBO in BYTES; we apply the >>4 and
217	// the swizzle field. Use the make_desc_*_kmajor convenience wrappers unless
218	// you have a bespoke smem layout.
219	template <SwizzleMode Swizzle = kSwizzleNone>
220	__device__ __forceinline__ SmemDesc make_smem_desc(
221	    const void* smem_base, uint32_t lbo_bytes, uint32_t sbo_bytes,
222	    uint32_t base_offset = 0u
223	) {
224	    SmemDesc d;
225	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 900)
226	    uint64_t addr = static_cast<uint64_t>(smem_desc_encode_addr(smem_base));
227	    uint64_t lbo  = static_cast<uint64_t>((lbo_bytes >> 4) & 0x3FFFu);
228	    uint64_t sbo  = static_cast<uint64_t>((sbo_bytes >> 4) & 0x3FFFu);
229	    uint64_t bo   = static_cast<uint64_t>(base_offset & 0x7u);
230	    uint64_t sw   = static_cast<uint64_t>(Swizzle & 0x3u);
231	    d.desc = (addr)                 // bits 13:0
232	           | (lbo << 16)            // bits 29:16
233	           | (sbo << 32)            // bits 45:32
234	           | (bo  << 49)            // bits 51:49
235	           | (sw  << 62);           // bits 63:62
236	#else
237	    (void)smem_base; (void)lbo_bytes; (void)sbo_bytes; (void)base_offset;
238	    d.desc = 0;
239	#endif
240	    return d;
241	}

291	//  fp32 accumulator fragment for an m64×N output tile.
292	//  PTX ISA §<ip>.3 "Register fragment for .f32 accumulators" (the
293	//  m64nNk16 wgmma writes its output across the 128 warpgroup threads).
294	//
295	//  Fragment layout (the ISA figure, decoded):
296	//    - 128 threads = 4 warps; the M=64 rows are split so that
297	//        warp w  (w in 0..3)  owns rows  [16*w .. 16*w+15],
298	//      and within a warp, lane L owns two row-groups:
299	//        row_hi = 16*w + (L/4)        (rows 0..7 of the warp's block)
300	//        row_lo = row_hi + 8          (rows 8..15)
301	//    - The N columns are held as N/2 fp32 registers per thread, in pairs:
302	//        register pair (2c, 2c+1) holds columns (col_base+0, col_base+1)
303	//        where col_base = (L%4)*2 + 8*(c/2_grouped)...  [the (col%8) + 8*(c>>1)
304	//      grouping of the ISA]. We expose the exact decode via frag_row()/
305	//      frag_col() so the epilogue (and the self-test) maps register i of
306	//      lane L (in warp w) to the (row,col) of the 64×N output it represents.
307	//
308	//  We store N/2 floats. c[2*g + p] is the p-th (p in {0,1}) of register-group
309	//  g (g in [0, N/4) for the "even/odd column pair" grouping). The helpers
310	//  frag_row(lane,i) / frag_col(lane,i) give the global (row,col) so a single
311	//  authoritative decode is shared by the epilogue store AND the gate's
312	//  reference comparison (no chance of a mismatched private decode).
313	// =========================================================================
314	template <int N>
315	struct WgmmaAccum {
316	    static_assert(N % 8 == 0, "wgmma N must be a multiple of 8");
317	    static constexpr int kRegs = N / 2;   // fp32 regs per thread
318	    float c[kRegs];
319	
320	    __device__ __forceinline__ void zero() {
321	        #pragma unroll
322	        for (int i = 0; i < kRegs; ++i) c[i] = 0.0f;
323	    }
324	};

326	// --- Authoritative fragment decode (PTX ISA §<ip>.3, .f32 accumulators) -
327	// For thread `tid_in_wg` in [0,128) and register index `i` in [0, N/2):
328	//   warp = tid_in_wg / 32 ; lane = tid_in_wg % 32.
329	//   The 64 M-rows are partitioned warp-major: rows [16*warp, 16*warp+16).
330	//   lane bits decode within the warp's 16-row × N block as in the ISA figure:
331	//     group g = i / 2 ; sub p = i % 2.
332	//     row = 16*warp + (lane / 4) + 8 * (g % 2 == 0 ? 0 : 0)   -- see below.
333	//
334	// The ISA C-fragment for .m64nNk16.f32 lays out each lane's N/2 elements as
335	// (over the row pair r0=lane/4, r1=r0+8) interleaved column pairs. The precise
336	// closed form, validated by the A=I gate, is:
337	//   group_of_8 = i / 8 ;   within = i % 8
338	//   row = 16*warp + (lane/4) + 8*(within / 4)
339	//   col = (lane%4)*2 + (within % 2) + 8*group_of_8 + ...
340	// To keep ONE source of truth that the gate verifies bit-for-bit, the decode
341	// is implemented below in the exact factored form the ISA figure gives for
342	// the 16x8 sub-blocks the f32 accumulator tiles across N.
343	__device__ __forceinline__ void wgmma_frag_decode(
344	    int tid_in_wg, int i, int N, int& row, int& col
345	) {
346	    const int warp = tid_in_wg >> 5;       // 0..3
347	    const int lane = tid_in_wg & 31;       // 0..31
348	    // Each 16x8 output sub-block (one "n8" column slab) contributes 4 regs
349	    // per thread (8 rows split into 2 row-halves × ... ). The ISA's .f32
350	    // fragment for an n8 slab gives, per lane:
351	    //   reg 0 -> (row = lane/4,       col = (lane%4)*2 + 0)
352	    //   reg 1 -> (row = lane/4,       col = (lane%4)*2 + 1)
353	    //   reg 2 -> (row = lane/4 + 8,   col = (lane%4)*2 + 0)
354	    //   reg 3 -> (row = lane/4 + 8,   col = (lane%4)*2 + 1)
355	    // and successive n8 slabs add 8 to the column. With N columns there are
356	    // N/8 slabs × 4 regs = N/2 regs (matches kRegs).
357	    const int slab   = i >> 2;             // which n8 column slab (0..N/8-1)
358	    const int within = i & 3;              // 0..3 within the slab
359	    const int row_half = within >> 1;      // 0 -> rows 0..7, 1 -> rows 8..15
360	    const int col_par  = within & 1;       // 0 or 1 column within the pair
361	    row = 16 * warp + (lane >> 2) + 8 * row_half;
362	    col = (lane & 3) * 2 + col_par + 8 * slab;
363	    (void)N;
364	}

596	//

598	//  determinism rule: one CTA owns the tile end-to-end, k ascending, no
599	//  work-steal split, no float atomics → bitwise-reproducible). The FIRST
600	//  issue uses ScaleD=0 (overwrite, so the accumulator need not be pre-zeroed
601	//  for a fresh tile); subsequent issues accumulate (ScaleD=1). One
602	//  wgmma_fence() before the group, one commit_group()+wait_group<0>() after.
603	//
604	//  `gen` is a functor: gen(k) -> {descA, descB} for k-step k (the caller
605	//  advances the smem base / pipeline stage between k-steps). Keeping the
606	//  descriptor generation a callback is what lets the SAME mainloop serve the
607	//  unpipelined gate (gen reads a fixed pre-staged tile array) and the
608	//  pipelined gate (gen reads the current ring-buffer stage) with bit-identical

612	//  with non-wgmma code (zero(), or a partial from a previous chain it wants to
613	//  ACCUMULATE onto), it must call wgmma_fence() itself and pass
614	//  FenceBeforeFirst=false + start with ScaleD=1. The default
615	//  (FenceBeforeFirst=true, first issue ScaleD=0) is the fresh-tile case.
616	// =========================================================================
617	template <int N, int TransA, int TransB, bool FenceBeforeFirst = true,
618	          typename DescGen>

620	    WgmmaAccum<N>& acc, int k_steps, DescGen gen
621	) {
622	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 900)
623	    if (FenceBeforeFirst) wgmma_fence();
624	    // First k-step OVERWRITES (ScaleD=0) so a fresh accumulator is correct
625	    // without a separate zero. (If the caller wants to accumulate onto a
626	    // pre-existing fp32 value, it sets FenceBeforeFirst=false, zeroes/sets the
627	    // accumulator + fences itself, and we still issue k=0 below — but then the
628	    // caller should pass an accumulating first step; for the common fresh-tile
629	    // path this is exactly D = sum_k A_k B_k.)
630	    {
631	        auto d = gen(0);
632	        wgmma_m64nNk16_bf16<N, /*ScaleD=*/0, TransA, TransB>(acc, d.first, d.second);
633	    }
634	    #pragma unroll 1
635	    for (int k = 1; k < k_steps; ++k) {
636	        auto d = gen(k);
637	        wgmma_m64nNk16_bf16<N, /*ScaleD=*/1, TransA, TransB>(acc, d.first, d.second);
638	    }

643	#endif

222	    constexpr int kVec = 16 / (int)sizeof(__nv_bfloat16);   // 8 bf16 / 16B

233	    constexpr int kBHalves = N * (kWgmmaAtomK / kVec);      // N*2

253	    // arrive happens-after its own cp.async + wait_group<0>, so the phase-flip

301	        #pragma unroll
302	        for (int s = 0; s < Depth; ++s) empty_parity[s] = 0u;
303	        for (int k = 0; k < k_steps; ++k) {

306	            // consumer released it (empty barrier) before overwriting.

315	        // fragment accumulates across the whole chain (first k overwrites).
316	        WgmmaAccum<N> acc;
317	        unsigned full_parity[Depth];
318	        #pragma unroll
319	        for (int s = 0; s < Depth; ++s) full_parity[s] = 0u;
320	
321	        // We can't use the kchain helper directly (it expects all descriptors
322	        // available); instead we inline the SAME choreography: one fence, then
323	        // k=0 overwrite / k>0 accumulate, commit+wait at the end. Issuing each
324	        // wgmma right after its stage is ready overlaps load and compute.
325	        wgmma_fence();
326	        for (int k = 0; k < k_steps; ++k) {

340	            }
341	            // Commit + wait THIS issue before releasing the slot, so the
342	            // producer does not overwrite operands the async wgmma still reads.
343	            wgmma_commit_group();
344	            wgmma_wait_group<0>();
345	            // Release the slot back to the producer. ALL 128 consumer threads
346	            // arrive (barrier count=128) — see init_barriers: the per-warp elect
347	            // would give 4 arrivals on a count-1 barrier and deadlock.
348	            pipe.empty(slot).arrive();
349	        }

352	        // output; decode relative to its 128-thread group (tid-128).
353	        const int tid_in_wg = threadIdx.x - 128;
354	        #pragma unroll
355	        for (int i = 0; i < WgmmaAccum<N>::kRegs; ++i) {
356	            int row, col;
357	            wgmma_frag_decode(tid_in_wg, i, N, row, col);
358	            gD[row * N + col] = acc.c[i];
359	        }
360	    }
361	#else
362	    (void)gA; (void)gB; (void)gD; (void)k_steps;
363	#endif

130	//  PREVIOUS one. The sense-reversing generation fixes this: each CTA samples
131	//  the generation on entry, then waits until the generation has ADVANCED
132	//  (the last arriver advances it), never touching `arrived` for reset on the
133	//  consumer side. The last CTA to arrive resets `arrived` to 0 and bumps the
134	//  generation in one release; everyone else spins on the generation.

138	//      must be visible to peers AFTER the barrier. We publish arrival with a
139	//      __threadfence() (device-scope release) before the atomicAdd, and the
140	//      waiters do an acquire by reading the generation with volatile semantics

143	//

145	//  of the block is gated by a __syncthreads() so the whole CTA leaves together.

177	                // then a release-store of the advanced generation so a CTA that
178	                // sees the new generation also sees arrived==0 when it next
179	                // enters. atomicExch gives the store device-scope visibility.
180	                atomicExch(g_arrived, 0u);

186	                // memory subsystem with the generation poll and steals issue

188	                // for an exponentially-growing nap (capped) so the poll rate

204	            // the peers' phase writes (released above) are visible to us.

213	    //   fwd → sync → reset_counter → sync → bwd → sync → reset_counter → sync

## 3. The TMA-descriptor HOST seam to reuse (cuTensorMapEncode / make_tma_copy)
================================================================================

CRITICAL FINDING: **there is currently NO TMA anywhere in the codebase's device path.** Grep for
`cuTensorMapEncode|CUtensorMap|make_tma_copy|cp.async.bulk` over `csrc/` (excluding third_party)
returns ONLY doc comments in mma.cuh (mma.cuh:91-92,102,108,222,462 describe what CUTLASS does
*internally*) and warp_specialize.cuh:10,65 (doc). The persistent megakernel stages operands with
**Ampere `cp.async`** (`cp.async.cg.shared.global`, primitives.cuh:497-508), NOT TMA. TMA is
explicitly deferred: tile_pipeline.cuh:199 *"this uses cp.async (.cg.16), NOT TMA — DESIGN §4.1 item
3 makes TMA explicitly phase-2"*; model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:783 *"needs TMA-with-transpose; out of
scope"*. So the rewrite is the FIRST place TMA enters the device path — there is no existing TMA
host seam to reuse; it must be BUILT, but CuTe provides the builder.

### The reuse path CuTe gives (the descriptor is a HOST-built `CUtensorMap`, device-consumed):
- `make_tma_copy(CopyOp, gtensor, slayout, ...)` is `CUTE_HOST_RTC` (host-only)
  (copy_traits_sm90_tma.hpp:1266, 1296, 1310; the A/B helpers `make_tma_copy_A_sm90` /
  `make_tma_copy_B_sm90` at 1458/1497). It internally calls `detail::make_tma_copy_desc`
  (copy_traits_sm90_tma.hpp:1108) which builds a `TmaDescriptor tma_desc{}` (= `CUtensorMap`) via the
  driver `cuTensorMapEncode*` path (copy_traits_sm90_tma.hpp:991-1066, fields:
  `to_CUtensorMapDataType<bf16>`, gmem shape/stride, box, swizzle).
- The resulting `TiledCopy`/`Copy_Atom` stores `TmaDescriptor tma_desc_` and exposes
  `get_tma_descriptor()` → `TmaDescriptor const*` (copy_traits_sm90_tma.hpp:109/115-116,
  241/247-248). The device-side `copy()` (SM90_TMA_LOAD::copy, copy_sm90_tma.hpp:277-312) takes
  `void const* desc_ptr` (= that pointer) + `uint64_t* mbar_ptr` (an mbarrier in smem) + smem dst +
  tile coords, and issues `cp.async.bulk.tensor.Nd.shared::cluster.global.mbarrier::complete_tx::bytes`.

### THE SEAM (matches the model's stable-buffer/operator-cache philosophy in mma.cuh:105-117):
A `CUtensorMap` encodes the tensor's GLOBAL BASE ADDRESS + shape/stride/box (mma.cuh:106-117
documents this exact invariant for the operator cache). So the host launcher of the megakernel must,
BEFORE the persistent launch, build one `CUtensorMap` per GEMM operand tensor (A acts, B weights, per
distinct {ptr, M/N/K, stride}) and pass the descriptor(s) into the kernel — by value in the launch
arg (the driver supports passing a `CUtensorMap` kernel param) or as a `__grid_constant__ const
CUtensorMap` / a device-global the kernel reads. Because the megakernel's param/weight/act buffers
are allocated ONCE and keep their address across steps (mma.cuh:110-117 "allocated ONCE and keep the
same address every step"), the descriptor is stable and can be built once and reused, mirroring the
mma.cuh operator cache rationale.
PerSistentContext (megakernel_common.cuh:263-276) is the natural place to add `const CUtensorMap*`
(or by-value descriptors) alongside `g_next_task/g_arrived/g_generation`.

CAVEAT: `make_tma_copy` wants the smem layout (`slayout`) it will scatter into = a CuTe swizzle
atom layout (see §4). The host build of the descriptor and the device smem layout MUST be the same
CuTe `Layout` instance/type → keep them in a shared `using` in the new header so host + device agree.

================================================================================
## 4. The CuTe DEVICE-SIDE atoms + the canonical reference pattern to replicate
================================================================================

The device rewrite replicates EXACTLY what CUTLASS's own SS-warpspecialized collective does in its
device `load()`/`mma()` methods — `sm90_mma_tma_gmma_ss_warpspecialized.hpp` is the ground-truth
device pattern (read in full, lines 300-575). The persistent kernel calls a hand-composed version of
this between GridBarriers.

### Atoms/types (all device-instantiable, header paths):
- **MMA atom**: `SM90_64xNx16_F32BF16BF16_SS` family in `cute/arch/mma_sm90_gmma.hpp`
  (declarations at lines 2247(N=8), 2338(16), 2433(32), 2538(64), 2663(96), 2808(128), 2973(192),
  3178(256)). Selected device-side by `GMMA::ss_op_selector<ElementA=bfloat16_t, ElementB=bfloat16_t,
  ElementC=float, TileShape_MNK, MajorA=K, MajorB=K>()` — `CUTE_HOST_DEVICE constexpr`
  (`cute/arch/mma_sm90.hpp:364-366`; requires Tile_M%64==0, Tile_K%16==0, mma_sm90.hpp:368-378).
  This is the CuTe analogue of wgmma.cuh's `wgmma_issue_n{8..128}` overloads (wgmma.cuh:443-561) —
  but the atom's `fma(desc_a, desc_b, accum, scale_D)` issues the same
  `wgmma.mma_async.sync.aligned.m64nNk16.f32.bf16.bf16` PTX (mma_sm90_gmma.hpp around each struct).
- **GMMA smem descriptor**: built automatically by CuTe from a swizzle smem layout via
  `make_gmma_desc<Major::K>(smem_tensor)` (`cute/atom/mma_traits_sm90_gmma.hpp:198-340`,
  `GmmaDescriptor` struct). This REPLACES the hand-packed 64-bit descriptor in wgmma.cuh
  (`make_smem_desc` / `make_desc_{A,B}_kmajor`, wgmma.cuh:219-288, and the manual bit layout
  wgmma.cuh:191-241). The hand-rolled LBO=MN*16/SBO=128 NONE-swizzle layout (wgmma.cuh:261-269) is
  exactly `GMMA::Layout_K_INTER_Atom<bf16>`; the perf path's swizzle is
  `GMMA::Layout_K_SW128_Atom<bf16>` etc. CuTe computes the descriptor bits + handles swizzle
  automatically — this is the "CuTe swizzle layouts" the goal wants.
- **TMA load atom**: `SM90_TMA_LOAD` (`cute/arch/copy_sm90_tma.hpp:277`), device `copy(desc_ptr,
  mbar_ptr, cache_hint, smem_ptr, crd...)` (copy_sm90_tma.hpp:280-312). Composed by `make_tma_copy`
  (§3) into a `TiledCopy` whose `.with(mbar, mask)` + `partition_S/partition_D` give the device copy
  (ss_warpspecialized.hpp:382-383).
- **Pipeline**: `cutlass::PipelineTmaAsync<Stages>` (`cutlass/pipeline/sm90_pipeline.hpp:271`).
  Device-constructible from `SharedStorage& + Params{role, is_leader, num_consumers, ...} +
  ClusterShape` (sm90_pipeline.hpp:292-296, 323-378). **Works with cluster_size==1**
  (sm90_pipeline.hpp:311,344) — the persistent-kernel case (ClusterShape `_1,_1,_1`). Device API:
  `producer_acquire`, `producer_get_barrier`, `consumer_try_wait`, `consumer_wait`,
  `consumer_release`, `producer_tail` (ss_warpspecialized.hpp:372-572). This REPLACES the hand-rolled
  Mbarrier ring in tile_pipeline.cuh (TilePipeline, warp_specialize.cuh Mbarrier).

### The device control flow to replicate (ss_warpspecialized.hpp):
PRODUCER `load()` (308-390): `elect_one_sync()`; per k-tile `pipeline.producer_acquire(write)`;
`copy(tma_load_a.with(*tma_barrier,mask), tAgA(...,*k_tile), tAsA(...,stage))` (+B); `++k_tile;
++write`. CONSUMER `mma()` (415-557): partition smem→fragments (`make_fragment_A/B`); per k-tile
`consumer_try_wait`+`consumer_wait`; `warpgroup_arrive()`; `cute::gemm(tiled_mma, tCrA(...), tCrB(...),
accum)` (algorithm/gemm.hpp:83); `warpgroup_commit_batch()`; `warpgroup_wait<K_PIPE_MMAS>()`;
`consumer_release(release)`. Warpgroup fence/commit/wait helpers live in `cute/arch/mma_sm90_gmma.hpp`
(`warpgroup_arrive`:49, `warpgroup_wait<N>`:62, `warpgroup_commit_batch`:76, `warpgroup_fence_operand`:88/99)
— the CuTe analogues of wgmma.cuh's `wgmma_fence/commit_group/wait_group` (wgmma.cuh:374-403).

================================================================================
## 5. HARD CONSTRAINTS — how the CuTe rewrite preserves them
================================================================================

### (a) 1-CTA/SM persistent + hand-built GridBarrier (NO cooperative launch):
The CuTe device pieces are all composable INSIDE the existing `__global__
fused_decoder_megakernel_tc` (fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:673, `__launch_bounds__(SG_TC_MEGA_BLOCK=256)`,
fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:348). The GEMM is invoked BETWEEN `bar.sync()` calls
(fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:818,877,913,953,...). `PipelineTmaAsync` + `ss_op_selector` + `SM90_TMA_LOAD`
are device functions/constructs — they do NOT launch a grid, so they slot in unchanged. ClusterShape
must stay `_1,_1,_1` (no cluster — keeps GridBarrier valid, megakernel_common.cuh:29 "needs NO
cooperative launch"). The host launcher builds the TMA descriptor(s) pre-launch (§3) and the plain
`<<<grid,block>>>` launch (fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:331) is unchanged.

### (b) ascending-k fp32 reduction order (A/A/A bit-determinism):
CUTLASS's mma() iterates k-tiles with `CUTLASS_PRAGMA_NO_UNROLL for (; k_tile_count>0; --k_tile_count)`
in ASCENDING k_tile order (ss_warpspecialized.hpp:526-554), with first k-tile `ScaleOut::Zero`
(overwrite) then `ScaleOut::One` (accumulate) (ss_warpspecialized.hpp:480,489,495,503) — IDENTICAL to
the hand-rolled `wgmma_mainloop_kchain` (wgmma.cuh:617-644: first ScaleD=0, rest ScaleD=1, ascending k)
and the decoder's `issue_k` (model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:759-760). The wgmma hardware accumulates each
m64nNk16 tile into the same fp32 fragment in issue order; ascending-k issue ⇒ same reduction order ⇒
the parity/determinism invariant holds BY CONSTRUCTION (model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:170-172,248,
"ascending-k, k=0 overwrite / k>0 accumulate ... fp32 accumulation order is bit-identical → fp64-oracle
parity + A/A/A determinism hold"). RISK: must keep ClusterShape=1, single consumer warpgroup per tile,
NO split-K / NO multi-CTA reduce (any cross-CTA float reduce changes order) — the existing G==1
single-CTA-per-tile path (model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:88-97) is the invariant to keep.

### (c) fp64 parity gate (rel 1e-4):
The parity gate compares the bf16-wgmma result against an fp64 oracle at rel 1e-4
(model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:124,171-172; referenced across the fused stages). Since the CuTe path uses
the SAME m64nNk16 bf16→fp32 atom and the SAME ascending-k order, it produces bit-identical results to
the hand-rolled engine (the atom IS the same PTX instruction). Parity is preserved as long as:
operand bf16 rounding is unchanged (same Major-K layout values), accumulation order unchanged (§b),
and no TF32/alternate-precision substitution sneaks in (keep `F32BF16BF16_SS`, NOT a TF32 atom).

================================================================================
## 6. CONCRETE rewrite shape (what the new header does, and the exact atoms/headers)
================================================================================

New device header (replacing wgmma.cuh's role inside the megakernel; keep wgmma.cuh as #ifndef
WITH_CUTLASS fallback for build matrix):
1. `using TileShape = Shape<_64, Int<N>, _16>` (N ∈ {64,96,128}); `using SmemLayoutAtomA/B =
   GMMA::Layout_K_INTER_Atom<bfloat16_t>` (correctness, NONE-swizzle == today's wgmma.cuh:261-269) or
   `GMMA::Layout_K_SW128_Atom<bfloat16_t>` (perf-phase swizzle).
2. `auto mma_atom = GMMA::ss_op_selector<bfloat16_t,bfloat16_t,float, TileShape, GMMA::Major::K,
   GMMA::Major::K>();` then `TiledMMA = make_tiled_mma(mma_atom)` (one warpgroup).
3. Host (in the megakernel launcher): `make_tma_copy(SM90_TMA_LOAD{}, gA_tensor, SmemLayoutA{}...)` /
   B → store `get_tma_descriptor()` pointer into PersistentContext.
4. Device, between barriers: build `Tensor sA/sB = make_tensor(make_smem_ptr(smem), SmemLayout{})`;
   construct `PipelineTmaAsync<Stages>(smem_storage, params{role,is_leader,num_consumers},
   ClusterShape_1_1_1)`; run the load()/mma() choreography (ss_warpspecialized.hpp:308-557 pattern),
   first-k `ScaleOut::Zero`, ascending k; epilogue: store accum fragment (CuTe partition replaces the
   hand decode wgmma.cuh:343-364 / model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:357-358).
5. Keep `__shared__` budget under the megakernel's 48KB static cap (fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:427-429;
   DecTcSmem ~17.5KB today, fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:355-364) OR opt into dynamic smem via
   `cudaFuncAttributeMaxDynamicSharedMemorySize` (the occupancy≥1 GridBarrier hang-freedom guard
   fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:309-321 must be re-checked with the new smem size, since 1 CTA/SM must
   still place).

KEY RISK/CONSTRAINT: the megakernel's 256-thread layout (2 warp-groups) must map to the
producer(TMA)/consumer(MMA) warp-spec the CuTe pipeline expects (PipelineTmaAsync Params.role,
num_consumers; sm90_pipeline.hpp:292-296). The TC megakernel currently runs wgmma on threads 0..127
with NO asymmetric setmaxnreg (fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:343-348) — adopting a producer/consumer
split (like tile_pipeline.cuh) is the natural fit for the CuTe pipeline but is a layout change to
validate against the parity gate.
